title: Senior's toolkit: calling APIs from the shell
summary: curl, HTTPie and jq: the commands integration engineers use to poke a gateway, a route or a backend directly.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: calling APIs from the shell
steps.body: When something between the client and the backend misbehaves, call each hop yourself: the gateway, the integration route, the backend. These commands tell you which one is wrong.

toolkit.what: Prints the status line and response headers before the body. Most integration bugs show up in headers: a wrong `Content-Type`, a leaked internal header, a `Location` pointing inside the network.
flags: no progress bar, but still print errors
toolkit.when: the first call to any endpoint you are debugging

toolkit.what: Sends a request body from a file, so you can replay the exact payload from a bug report.
flags: body from a file (`--data-binary @f` keeps newlines exactly)
same, and sets `Content-Type` and `Accept` to JSON (curl 7.82+)

toolkit.what: Exits non-zero on a 4xx or 5xx but still prints the error body. Plain curl exits 0 on a 500, which hides failures in scripts.
flags: fail on HTTP errors and keep the body (curl 7.76+)
fail on HTTP errors and drop the body
toolkit.when: every curl in a script, a health check or a pipeline

toolkit.what: Prints chosen facts about the call, such as the status and how long it took, instead of the body.
toolkit.when: comparing the gateway hop with a direct call to the backend

toolkit.what: Shows the whole conversation: which address it connected to, the TLS handshake, every request and response header.
flags: verbose; lines starting with `>` were sent, `<` were received
skip certificate checks (local debugging only, never in code)

toolkit.what: A friendlier HTTP client: JSON by default, coloured output, short syntax for fields and headers.
flags: a string field in the JSON body
a raw JSON value (number, bool, array)

toolkit.what: Filters and reshapes JSON on the command line, so a 2,000-line response becomes the three fields you care about.
flags: walk into arrays and pick a field
raw strings, no quotes (for use in scripts)

steps.prompt: Match each curl option to what it does.
pairs: print the response headers before the body
send the body from a file
exit non-zero on 4xx/5xx and still print the body
print the status code after the call
show the connection, TLS and every header

steps.prompt: Print only the ids of failed orders, one per line, without quotes.
steps.explain: `-r` prints raw strings, so a script can loop over the ids. `select(cond)` keeps only the items where the condition is true.

steps.prompt: A client gets `502 Bad Gateway` from `https://gateway.example.com/orders/42`. You are on a host that can reach both the gateway and the orders backend. What do you do first?
options: Call the backend directly with `curl -i` and compare it with the same call through the gateway
Raise the gateway timeout to 60 seconds
steps.explain: A 502 means the gateway could not get a valid answer from the next hop. Calling each hop yourself tells you whether the backend is down, slow, or answering in a way the gateway rejects. Changing settings before you know which hop fails is guessing.

steps.prompt: A deploy script runs `curl -sS http://orders:8080/health` and carries on. Yesterday the service returned 503 and the deploy still went ahead. What is the smallest fix?
options: Add `--fail-with-body` (or `-f`) so curl exits non-zero on a 4xx or 5xx
Add `-v` so the status is printed
Add `-i` so the headers are printed
steps.explain: Without `-f` or `--fail-with-body`, curl only fails when it cannot connect. Any HTTP status, even 503, counts as success. Printing more output does not stop the script.

steps.prompt: Which tool would you reach for?
items: Replay a bug report's payload exactly from a file in a CI script
See the TLS handshake and every header of a failing call
Quickly try a POST with a few JSON fields by hand
Send `qty` as the number 2, not the string "2", with short syntax
Pull one field out of a large JSON response
Keep only the items whose status is FAILED

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Before you open the gateway console or the code, call the failing endpoint yourself with `curl -i`, then call the hop behind it. Put `--fail-with-body` on every curl in a script, and paste the exact curl command into tickets so others can reproduce what you saw.
